sections.title: Positioning
sections.summary: Smile sells loyalty to ambitious Shopify brands with one specific outcome: more second orders. The site now leads with Shopify Plus and enterprise customers.
keyPoints: Homepage: 'Loyalty that drives second orders', cycling through repeat revenue, lifetime value and higher AOV.
'The loyalty platform for ambitious Shopify brands. Join thousands on Shopify Plus accelerating growth through modern loyalty programs.'
A section asks 'Switching from Yotpo, LoyaltyLion, Rivo, or Okendo?', naming four rivals.
Enterprise credentials are prominent: certified by Shopify and independently audited with SOC 2 Type II.

sections.title: Products and offerings
sections.summary: A loyalty platform built on points, VIP tiers and referrals, with newer modules for cashback and bonus events, and deep Shopify and Klaviyo integration.

rows: The core loyalty program, fully embedded in the storefront
Store credit in the brand's name held in Shopify, spent online, in store and in the Shop app
Short, time-bound bonus points and multipliers measured in sales
Points redeemed at Shopify Plus checkout and earned in store
A branded loyalty page and hub for members
Loyalty data on every profile and pre-built flows for points, tiers and referrals
Build loyalty into custom storefronts and apps

sections.title: Pricing
sections.summary: Published plans on the 'For Scale' tab, priced by monthly orders with a clear overage rate. Enterprise is custom, and a separate 'For Startups' tab was not read.
keyPoints: All plans lead with 'Book a demo'; no self-serve checkout is offered.
Growth is billed monthly; Plus and Enterprise are billed annually.
Extra orders cost $20 per 100 on Growth and $5 per 100 on Plus.
Enterprise is for retailers with over $40M in annual revenue, with advanced security and 99.9% historical uptime.
The page notes prices are in USD and were reviewed as of September 25, 2026.

rows: VIP program, Loyalty Hub, fully embedded loyalty, performance benchmarks, 25 specialized reports
Migration and launch plan, quarterly program monitoring, priority support, API access, 30+ reports
Advanced security, 99.9% historical uptime, custom API rate limits, data warehouse sync

gaps: The 'For Startups' tab and its plans were not read.

sections.title: Merchandising
sections.summary: A usage-based ladder where the plan jump is tied to migration help, monitoring and API access, plus unusually concrete advice for merchants on how to merchandise loyalty itself.
keyPoints: Plans are scaled by monthly orders with an explicit overage rate, so cost tracks the merchant's size.
Higher plans add services (migration and launch plan, quarterly monitoring, priority support), not just features.
For merchants: bonus events to create short bursts with points instead of markdowns, cashback, VIP status, referrals and checkout redemption.
Industry pages (fashion and apparel, beauty, food and beverage, pet care) argue for rewarding full-price buying and giving customers status.
A Learn hub carries guides, comparisons and benchmark research on loyalty.

sections.title: Technical platform
sections.summary: A dedicated developer site with a guides section, an API reference, a JavaScript SDK and UI components, plus an llms.txt index; a headless option and a large integration directory support custom builds.
keyPoints: dev.smile.io describes 'Enterprise loyalty. Built for developers.' with Guides, API Reference, a JavaScript SDK and Smile UI.
The docs publish a documentation index at /llms.txt for machine readers.
A headless and JS SDK page, a Klaviyo integration and answers about Recharge and reviews apps show a connected stack.
Plus adds API access; Enterprise adds custom API rate limits and data warehouse sync.
gaps: API reference depth and webhooks were not read.

sections.title: Design
sections.summary: Quiet and editorial: a light grey canvas, a heavy black grotesque with a grey second line, soft rounded cards and photography. The developer site switches to a different type and blue.
keyPoints: Marketing pages use Stabil Grotesk on a light grey (#f4f4f5) background with black buttons and 14px corners.
A two-tone headline repeats the pattern: black first line, grey second line, on both the home and pricing pages.
The home page shows a strip of customer-brand photographs in rounded cards under the headline.
The developer site uses Inter with a blue (#1e38fb) on white.
Pages are compact: the home page is 5,824px tall and pricing 6,827px.
For merchants: 'Loyalty shaped like your brand. Made from the elements you choose', with embedded loyalty and a UI kit.

sections.title: Company presentation
sections.summary: A specialist's story: Shopify-only focus, enterprise credentials and customer results, with a dedicated team as the promise.
keyPoints: Smile Editions Fall 2026 announces 50+ product updates, mirroring Shopify's own Editions cadence.
'Enterprise-ready, by Shopify's own measure' and 'A dedicated team, not a ticket queue' are the trust claims.
Customer stories are 'Enterprise brands first', with Blue Banana among them.
A press kit gives logo and color guidance.
gaps: No About page or leadership information in the surveyed pages.

signupPath: No self-serve signup was found. Every plan on the pricing page and every call to action on the homepage is 'Book a demo' with the line '30 minutes with a loyalty strategist'. The booking form was not followed. Nothing was entered.

jtbd_fit.evidence: One job in the headline: second orders and repeat revenue.

capability_visible.evidence: Mockups and results are shown; trial and demo environments are not.

pricing_transparency.evidence: Growth and Plus prices, orders included and overage rates are published; Enterprise is custom and the startup tab was not read.

product_breadth.evidence: Points, VIP, referrals, cashback, bonus events, checkout and POS are each explained.

platform_depth.evidence: Developer site with API reference, JS SDK, UI kit and llms.txt; headless option.

time_to_value.evidence: Capture stops before the product; first-value time was not observed.

friction.evidence: The surveyed pages could not tell.

trust.evidence: Shopify certification, SOC 2 Type II and enterprise customer stories.

mobile.evidence: Phone captures exist for home and pricing but were not assessed.

states.evidence: No error or empty states reached.

value_prop_clarity.evidence: 'Loyalty that drives second orders' is specific and measurable.

proof_quality.evidence: Customer results are shown, but 'thousands on Shopify Plus' has no source.

persuasion_integrity.evidence: No urgency tactics; pricing carries a review date.

cta_logic.evidence: 'Book a demo' with '30 minutes with a loyalty strategist' is the one consistent action.

company_narrative.evidence: A Shopify-specialist and enterprise story across home, pricing, customers and docs.

offer_packaging.evidence: Three plans sized by monthly orders with overage rates; the startup tab sits behind a toggle.

offer_architecture.evidence: Usage-based ladder where higher plans add services and API access.

merchant_merch_tools.evidence: Points, VIP tiers, referrals, cashback, bonus events and checkout redemption with measurement.

visual_craft.evidence: Clean hierarchy, strong two-tone headline and brand photography.

system_coherence.evidence: Marketing pages are consistent; the developer site uses a different font and a blue accent.

merchant_design_control.evidence: Loyalty 'shaped like your brand', fully embedded, with a UI kit and branded cashback.

read.summary: A specialist loyalty platform with a precise promise, a published usage-based price list and, rare in this set, a lot of guidance on how merchants should merchandise rewards. It is sales-led throughout: there is no self-serve start.
pros: A one-line outcome promise: second orders.
Plan prices, order limits and overage rates are shown.
Merchants get bonus events, cashback, VIP tiers and checkout redemption with measurement.
Developer docs include an llms.txt index and a JS SDK.
cons: No self-serve start: every plan leads to 'Book a demo'.
The developer site looks different from the marketing site.
The 'For Startups' pricing tab sits behind a toggle.
read.howItSells: Sells a measurable outcome to Shopify Plus brands, with enterprise credentials, a named list of rivals and a team behind the product.
copy: Name the single outcome in the headline.
Publish overage rates beside included volume.
Offer short bonus events as a merchandising tool.
avoid: No way to try the product without a call.
A second visual system for developer pages.
unknowns: Customer stories beyond the headline results.

hypothesis.statement: Adding a self-serve sandbox with a sample program will raise qualified demo requests among visitors who want to see the product first.
hypothesis.decisionRule: Ship if qualified requests rise by a pre-agreed margin over four weeks.

merchandising.summary: A usage-based ladder and a deep set of loyalty merchandising tools with guidance on using them.
pros: Usage-based ladder with overage rates shown.
Services in the higher plans, not just features.
Guides on how to run bonus events.
cons: The startup tab is hidden behind a toggle.

design.summary: Calm, consistent and editorial on the main site; a separate look on the developer site.
pros: A confident two-tone headline and brand photography give the site an editorial feel.
The light grey canvas keeps focus on the content.
cons: The developer site switches font and accent.

claims.text: Join thousands on Shopify Plus accelerating growth through modern loyalty programs.
Prices in USD. Reviewed as of September 25, 2026.
